scope: Final audit of Batch 2 Phases 1 to 3 together: a whole-journey test, a frontend/backend contract test, and fixes for 17 confirmed defects including an approval bypass on production release, a cross-phase GitHub break, verification before any browser test passed, and an aborted QA run reported as passed. Nothing is applied, deployed or enabled and no external account was touched.

keep: Phases 1 to 3 as separate reviewable drafts
Canonical scheduler, engine, runtime and budget ledger
Source stored in Postgres through the transactional revision RPC
extend: Operation approval is scoped to provider and action
Verification state is earned by a passed browser test
Preview readiness is recorded per revision

schemaImpact.rollout: Additive nullable column on builder_projects with a CHECK on its shape. Depends on the Phase 1 migration. Not applied by this change.
schemaImpact.rollback: ALTER TABLE public.builder_projects DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS preview_readiness;

auth.description: New preview restart route requires the issued tenant context; a foreign project id returns 404.

tenant.description: No tenant boundary changes; every new query carries the verified owner.

approval.description: An operation can only be approved, cancelled or run through its own provider and action, closing a path that approved a production release with the plan digest alone.

credentials.description: The credential scan now also rejects Supabase secret keys, service-role JWTs (by role claim), AWS, Stripe and Slack keys before source is stored or exported.

egress.description: In production the in-process browser is off unless an operator opts in, so generated pages are not driven inside the privileged API container.

tests.scope: Whole journey across the three phases and a regression test for every audit defect.
Every Builder client call is a served route with the same method; panels are rendered; the router is authenticated.
The new migration and column, and the existing real-database and browser tests.

architecture.reason: Tightens the existing approval lifecycle, QA and state handling. No scheduler, runtime, browser stack, agent framework or authentication system is added.

rollout: Merge in order with the Batch 2 stack after review and your authorization; follow docs/infra/COMBINED-ACTIVATION-RUNBOOK.md. Nothing is activated by merging.
rollback: Disable NEXT_PUBLIC_XROGA_BUILDER; routes are inert without a project. Drop the nullable column with the statement above.
knownGaps: No live Google runtime, model build, GitHub, Supabase or Vercel verification
The in-process browser must move to an isolated host before production QA is on
No chat-to-project association and no builder cancel control
Vercel production address is the expected one; timeouts of deployment and env calls are not reconciled
placeholderClaimsRemaining: Live provider and Google-runtime behaviour is unverified

blockers: Migrations not applied and engine not enabled
No approved disposable GitHub, Supabase or Vercel accounts for live verification
Authenticated end-to-end and staged security proof not run for this change
